The drawing shows a 1,4-dihydropyridine ring with an N-acetyl group and a 2-(trifluoromethyl)phenyl substituent at C4.

**Ring.** The nitrogen carries the acetyl group, C(=O)CH3. From N, one side is N–CH=CH–C4 and the other side is N–CH=CH–C4. C4 is an sp3 CH attached to the aryl group, so both ring double bonds are C2=C3 and C5=C6.

**Aryl group.** The benzene ring is attached to C4 and has CF3 on the adjacent (ortho) carbon.

**SMILES.** The acetyl is CC(=O)N1, and the ring runs C=CC(Ar)C=C1. The aryl group is c1ccccc1C(F)(F)F, with the ring-closure carbon attached to C4 and the CF3-bearing carbon next to it.

Full SMILES: CC(=O)N1C=CC(C=C1)c1ccccc1C(F)(F)F

Atom check: the ring has N plus C=C, C4, and C=C, which makes 6 atoms. The ring closure is correct. C4 has no stereo, as it is not a stereocentre because the two ring arms are identical.

SMILES: CC(=O)N1C=CC(C=C1)c1ccccc1C(F)(F)F
